domazlice_1431.description: The Hussites arrive to relieve Domažlice and find the crusading army in confusion. Exploit its wavering morale.
domazlice_1431.historicalSignificance: The expedition’s collapse in 1431 accelerated the turn to negotiation. The chorale symbolises victory; it is not proven to be the sole cause of the flight.

briefing.hussites: You are coming to relieve besieged Domažlice. Enemy movements have caused confusion and fear of your arrival. Exploit the hesitation, but expect resistance. The game’s chorale is a morale mechanic, not the sole explanation of the historical flight.
briefing.crusaders: Hussites approach! Try to form defense, or at least safely retreat to Bavaria.

secondary: Relieve the approach to besieged Domažlice

debriefing.victory: The expedition withdrew and the route to Domažlice is open. Historically, confusion, troop movements and fear of the Hussites contributed to the army’s collapse, but there was still some fighting. The chorale became a symbol of victory; a song defeating an entire army without a fight is an oversimplification.
debriefing.defeat: Crusaders overcame their fear and formed defense. Despite your choral they didn't collapse. Hussite reputation of invincibility is shaken.

phases.name: Hussite march
phases.description: Hussites rapidly approach Domažlice.

events.message: Hussite army covered 80 km in 2 days and approaches Domažlice!

events.text: Scouts report: Hussites are closer than we expected!

phases.name: Confusion in the camp
phases.description: Troop movements, divided command and reports of the Hussite approach fuel panic.

events.text: Sound of choral terrifies crusaders!
events.message: The Hussite force is approaching. Movements inside the camp are being mistaken for the start of a retreat.

events.text: Confusion and fear weaken the crusading army’s morale.

events.message: Cardinal Cesarini flees and loses cardinal hat!

events.text: Panic spreads through crusader camp!

events.message: The crusaders hear the chorale and the rumble of wagons - and break into flight!
events.text: Fear of the Hussites and disrupted command spread panic, but some units may still resist.

phases.name: Flight to Bavaria
phases.description: Crusaders flee through Všeruby pass to Bavaria.

events.text: Entire crusader army breaks into flight!

oblehani_plzne_1433.name: Siege of Plzeň
oblehani_plzne_1433.description: A playable episode of the long siege of Plzeň: an attempt against the city defences, not a reconstruction of a documented general assault on a specific day.
oblehani_plzne_1433.historicalSignificance: Greatest Hussite failure. Plzeň resisted almost year and received camel in coat of arms.

briefing.hussites: After months of siege time for decisive assault! Break through walls and capture city. Prokop the Great watches from rear - mustn't fail!
briefing.crusaders: Hussites prepare general assault! Vilém Švihovský of Rýzmburk leads defense. Hold walls at all costs!

debriefing.victory: You broke into the city. Your game has departed from history: the siege of 1433–1434 ended in failure for the field armies. You captured the city positions, not the lost unity of the Hussite leagues.
debriefing.defeat: Plzeň held, as it did in the historical siege that ended on 9 May 1434. The long campaign weakened the field armies and deepened their crisis. The captured camel became a civic symbol; the people of Plzeň added it to their arms themselves, not as a reward granted by Sigismund.

phases.name: Artillery preparation
phases.description: Hussite guns bombard walls. Defenders respond from city positions.

events.message: Hussite bombards open fire on Plzeň walls!
Defenders take cover behind battlements. Vilém Švihovský encourages garrison.
First cracks appear in walls!

phases.name: Assault on walls
phases.description: Infantry advances to walls. Heavy losses on both sides.

events.message: Jan Pardus of Horka leads Taborite infantry to attack!
The defenders cover the approaches to the walls and repel the attacking infantry.
Bloody fighting at walls! Hussites try to break defense.

phases.name: Fight at the gates
phases.description: The garrison may attempt a sortie if it still has the strength. Fighting continues at the fortifications.

events.message: Vilém Švihovský prepares a sortie. The defenders still fit to fight gather near the gates.

events.text: The defenders still fit to fight near the gates gain confidence.

phases.name: Decision
phases.description: Attack either succeeds, or Hussites must retreat.

events.message: Last chance for breakthrough! Prokop the Great sends reserves.

events.text: Hunger, violent foraging in the countryside, and quarrels among the captains break the camp. Some soldiers desert.

lipany_1434.name: Battle of Lipany
lipany_1434.description: Fratricidal battle between Hussites. Moderate Utraquists and Catholics defeat radical Taborites and Orphans.
lipany_1434.historicalSignificance: Defeat of the radical field armies and the death of Prokop the Great: a major turning point, not the immediate end of all Hussite warfare.

briefing.hussites: As commander of radicals you must repel attack by moderates. Beware their trap - feigned retreat!
briefing.crusaders: You lead coalition of moderates. Use feigned retreat, lure radicals from wagon fort and strike from flank with cavalry.

objectives.primary: Hold wagon fort and destroy 50% of coalition

debriefing.victory: The field armies have won at Lipany and the coalition has been defeated. You won the battle that history lost — but the country remains divided. Military victory is not yet reconciliation.
debriefing.defeat: The field armies have been defeated at Lipany. The coalition has settled the battle in its favour; its victors will now negotiate the country's future from a position of strength.

texts.alive: Prokop the Great survived this battle. His later fate lies beyond this playthrough.
texts.fallen: Prokop the Great fell in this battle. Its outcome cannot undo his death.
texts.escaped: Prokop the Great fled the battlefield. He is not among the fallen, but no longer stands with his army at the battle's end.

phases.name: Stalemate
phases.description: Negotiations have failed. Former allies now face each other.

events.message: Fratricidal battle begins...
Negotiations have failed. Among those facing you are men who once fought under the same sign.

phases.name: Setting the trap
phases.description: The coalition seeks a chance to draw the field armies out of their defences.

events.message: The coalition is looking for a weak point in your defence. Beware of a feigned retreat!
The coalition is ordered to feign a retreat. Pursuit could open a path for its cavalry.

phases.name: The decisive clash
phases.description: Watch the cavalry; keeping your defence together may decide the battle.

events.message: The decisive clash. Watch the cavalry; whether to leave the wagon fort is your decision.

phases.name: The final stage
phases.description: The battle continues. Those who can still hold together will decide it.

events.message: The battle is nearing its end. What matters now is which troops can still hold together.

texts.alive: Prokop the Great is alive and still on the battlefield. The outcome is still being fought over.
texts.fallen: Prokop the Great has fallen in this battle. The remaining troops fight on without him.
texts.escaped: Prokop the Great has left the battlefield. The fighting continues without him.

sion_1437.name: Siege of Sion Castle
sion_1437.description: The closing stage of the siege of Sion. Jan Roháč of Dubá holds the fortified bailey and castle core against the royal army.
sion_1437.historicalSignificance: The fall of Sion and the execution of Jan Roháč and his companions in Prague on 9 September 1437 became a potent symbol of the suppression of armed resistance to Sigismund.

briefing.hussites: You have faced a royal siege since spring. Defend the three bailey banks and the castle core above the Vrchlice. Reinforcements increase the attackers’ pressure. Twelve game turns represent the closing stage, not the entire months-long siege.
briefing.crusaders: King Sigismund loses patience. With Hungarian reinforcements finally capture that cursed castle and take Roháč alive!

reinforcements.crusaders: Hungarian reinforcements of Michal Országh arrived!

debriefing.victory: Sion held in your game and Jan Roháč survived. This is a counterfactual outcome: the castle fell on 6 September 1437 and Roháč and his companions were executed in Prague three days later. Your victory changes this defence, not the historical siege.
debriefing.defeat: Sion’s defence has ended in your game. Historically, the castle fell on 6 September 1437; the captured Jan Roháč and his companions were executed in Prague on 9 September. Accounts differ on exact totals and dramatic details. Fortifications and ammunition finds indicate real fighting, not merely a staged siege.

phases.name: Siege positions
phases.description: The royal army presses the fortified bailey and castle core.

events.message: The siege has continued since spring. Artillery positions cover the castle from the north and south.
No well is documented, but protected access to the Vrchlice could supply water. Hold the defensive perimeter.
King Sigismund loses patience. Sends Hungarian army!

phases.name: Arrival of Hungarians
phases.description: Hungarian reinforcements change balance of power.

events.message: Michal Országh brings Hungarian knights! Situation desperate.

events.text: Hungarian knights encourage royal army to decisive attack!

phases.name: Final assault
phases.description: General assault on walls. Defenders fight for survival.

events.message: Guns bombard the defences. Holding the approaches to the castle core is crucial.

events.text: Some defenders lose hope. Jan Roháč encourages them to fight!

events.message: The attackers are seeking a way across the ditches. Watch the passages between the banks.

phases.name: Final resistance
phases.description: Holding the castle core will decide the outcome.

events.message: The approaches to the core are contested. Losing its key positions will end the defence.
The defence reaches its final stage. The garrison and held positions decide this battle, not a prewritten legend.

horice_1423.name: Battle of Hořice
horice_1423.description: Žižka’s army and wagons defend Gothard hill against Čeněk of Wartenberg’s forces. The defensive position offsets the enemy cavalry.
horice_1423.historicalSignificance: Decisive defeat of Catholic nobility in northeastern Bohemia. Hussites captured Catholic wagons and guns.

briefing.hussites: Lock the wagon fort on Gothard hill and place the guns inside it. The Lords' League under Čeněk of Wartenberg approaches with superior cavalry. Let the knights climb the slope, dismount, and tire — then break them with gunfire and charge downhill!
briefing.crusaders: Žižka's radicals have fortified the hill. The Lords' League has superior cavalry — crush them before they finish forming up!

debriefing.victory: The defence of Gothard held. Wagons, fire and the slope helped repel the attack in this battle. Historically, the victory strengthened Žižka’s position in eastern Bohemia; exact deployments and losses remain uncertain.
debriefing.defeat: Catholic superiority broke through. Gothard hill fell and with it hope of holding eastern Bohemia. Hussite forces scattered and Čeněk of Wartenberg celebrates victory.

phases.name: Taking positions
phases.description: Hussites fortify on Gothard hill, Catholics gather.

events.message: Žižka: "To the hill! Hold slopes, shooters forward!"
Catholic nobility forms for attack below hill.

phases.name: Frontal assault
phases.description: Čeněk of Wartenberg throws cavalry into frontal assault on hill.

events.message: Čeněk of Wartenberg: "Forward! Crush heretics!"
Heavy cavalry crashes into Hussite infantry! Attack bogs down on steep slope.

events.text: The lords must dismount - there is no charging uphill onto the wagons and pikes on horseback.

phases.name: Three-hour battle
phases.description: Furious fighting on Gothard slopes. Catholics suffer heavy losses.

events.message: Hussite hand cannons and shooters mow down attackers!
Arnošt Flaška's troop collapses under fire!

events.text: The collapse of Flaška's troop shook the Catholics.

phases.name: Hussite counterattack
phases.description: Žižka orders counterattack. Orebite cavalry and infantry charge from hill.

events.message: Žižka: "Now! Forward, for the chalice!"
Catholics break into flight! Čeněk flees with handful of men!

phases.name: Pursuit
phases.description: Hussites pursue fleeing Catholics and capture their wagons.

events.message: All Catholic wagons and guns captured!
Čeněk of Wartenberg escaped. Hussite victory is complete.

malesov_1424.name: Battle of Malešov
malesov_1424.description: Žižka’s army uses a defensive position against a coalition of Prague forces and nobles. Prepare to counterattack down the slope.
malesov_1424.historicalSignificance: A major victory for Žižka over a coalition of Prague forces and nobles. The precise battlefield and casualty totals remain disputed.

briefing.hussites: Anti-Žižka coalition caught up with you at Malešov. Use slope above Bohynka stream valley. Enemy has numerical superiority, but terrain is on your side!
briefing.crusaders: We finally caught up with Žižka! He has fewer men. We'll surge into valley and crush heretics once and for all!

objectives.primary: Advance down the slope and break the coalition line — occupy its position by turn 10

debriefing.victory: The coalition line is broken! Your advance down the slope succeeded. Historically, victory at Malešov opened Žižka’s way towards Kutná Hora. The later story of stone-filled wagons is not a securely documented explanation for that success.
debriefing.defeat: The coalition repelled your advance. Žižka’s eastern Bohemian army must withdraw. Your game has diverged from history; the name Orphans was adopted by some of his followers only after his death.

phases.name: Taking positions
phases.description: Žižka recognizes terrain with help of Roháč and Hvězda. Hussites fortify on slope.

events.message: Jan Roháč: "Lord captain, we have good slope above valley. Bohynka stream covers our center."
Jan Hvězda: "I know these places. Valley is narrow - enemy won't be able to deploy."

phases.name: Coalition attack
phases.description: Anti-Žižka coalition throws cavalry into valley. Enemy cannot fully deploy.

events.message: Čeněk of Wartenberg: "To attack! We'll crush the blind man once and for all!"
Heavy cavalry enters narrow valley... Ranks crowd!

events.text: Cavalry loses momentum in marshy valley!

phases.name: Bloody valley
phases.description: Fire and constricted terrain disrupt the attackers’ advance. The defenders look for a chance to counterattack.

events.message: Hand cannons and handguns fire into crowded enemy ranks!
Coalition losses grow! Valley colors with blood!

events.text: Coalition army loses courage in murderous fire.

events.title: Disrupted vanguard
events.text: Crowded units cannot deploy under fire. Confusion in the vanguard shakes the formations behind them.

phases.name: Žižka's counterattack
phases.description: Žižka orders deadly counterattack down slope.

events.message: Žižka: "Now! Down the hill! For God's truth!"
Hussite cavalry and infantry rush down slope at disoriented enemy!

events.text: Attack from hill! +15% to Hussite units' attack.

phases.name: Coalition collapse
phases.description: Coalition army collapses. Rear units flee without fight.

events.message: Coalition collapses! Men flee toward Malešov!
Čeněk of Wartenberg: "Back! Everyone back!" Rear units didn't even enter battle.
Unit cohesion will decide the outcome. Historical casualty estimates are not a count of losses in this game.
Žižka controls battlefield. Road to Kutná Hora open!

plzen.name: Siege of Plzeň

hussiteSide.strength: Combined field armies of Taborites and Orphans
hussiteSide.composition: Taborites, Orphans; reinforcements from Poland (Čapek of Sány)

enemySide.composition: Catholic Plzeň townsfolk, west-Bohemian Catholic nobility

plzen.terrain: A fortified town and siege works. Reconstructions differ on the numbers of towers and guns.

quotes.text: The siege of Pilsen lasted from 14 July 1433 to 9 May 1434, and the town held out.
quotes.source: Authored summary · references under History and sources

trivia: You play a compressed, undated assault episode. A match does not replay nine months in exact order, and a Hussite victory is an alternative outcome.
The captured camel became a town emblem. We do not claim Sigismund granted it: the town adopted the symbol itself and received later confirmation.
plzen.aftermath: The Hussites' greatest failure. The collapse of the field armies' unity led straight to Lipany.
plzen.reliability: Gun counts, individual sorties and assault formations require caution. Prokop represents the wider siege, not a confirmed presence in a particular assault.

sion.name: Siege of Sion Castle
sion.location: Sion near Chlístovice, above the Vrchlice valley

enemySide.strength: The land levy plus Hungarian troops
enemySide.composition: The army of Sigismund of Luxembourg, Prague burghers

sion.terrain: A rocky castle core above the Vrchlice, a larger bailey with three banks, and siege positions to the north and south.

quotes.text: The castle was besieged from May and taken on 6 September 1437. More recent archaeology documents siege firing positions and intense fighting.
quotes.source: Authored summary · references under History and sources

trivia: The map retains the relationship between the rocky core, bailey, triple banks and Vrchlice stream. Fortifications are compressed; deployments, reinforcement timing and the alternative outcome are gameplay reconstructions.
The older suggestion of a merely staged siege is not the current archaeological conclusion. It belongs to the history of interpretation, not proof that no fighting occurred.

casualties.hussites: Roháč and companions captured and executed; totals vary
casualties.enemy: Unknown; low losses cannot be inferred from a percentage of finds

sion.aftermath: Sion fell on 6 September 1437. Jan Roháč and his companions were executed in Prague on 9 September.
sion.reliability: How intense fighting was distributed over the siege remains uncertain. The absence of a well alone does not prove continuous thirst: the plan identifies protected access to water.

zatec.name: Defense of Žatec
zatec.location: Žatec - a promontory above the Ohře river, northwest Bohemia

hussiteSide.strength: Garrison of 5,400 foot and 400 horse + a mass of country folk
hussiteSide.composition: Town garrison; billmen, flailmen, crossbows and hook-guns

commanders: archbishops of Mainz, Cologne and Trier
enemySide.composition: The Second Crusade - imperial princes, cavalry, siege guns

zatec.terrain: A mighty fortress on a promontory encircled on three sides by the Ohře. Assault was possible from only one side.

quotes.text: Žatec withstood the second crusade’s siege in September and early October 1421. The town community and garrison held the defences.
quotes.source: Authored summary · references under History and sources

trivia: One assault sector and a fixed turn count condense the siege. This is not a complete plan of the town’s fortifications.

Erkinger’s association with fighting at Žatec in 1420 does not establish his precise role in 1421. He is the game’s chosen representative of the besiegers. Numbers and individual assaults are reconstructed.

casualties.hussites: Low - the town was well provisioned
casualties.enemy: Considerable; plus hunger in the camp

zatec.aftermath: The Second Crusade fell apart without ever meeting Žižka in the field.
zatec.reliability: Erkinger’s association with fighting at Žatec in 1420 does not establish his precise role in 1421. He is the game’s chosen representative of the besiegers. Numbers and individual assaults are reconstructed.

zivohost.name: Battle of Živohošť
zivohost.location: Area between Živohošť and Nový Knín

enemySide.composition: Heavy cavalry of Czech Catholic nobility

zivohost.terrain: High ground near Vltava crossing. Wagon fort was NOT used.
zivohost.outcome: Indecisive battle. Showed necessity of organized defense.
zivohost.aftermath: Indecisive battle. Showed necessity of organized defense.
zivohost.significance: Historically the FIRST major clash of the Hussite Wars. Demonstrated that pilgrims needed better organization and tactics.

quotes.text: The clash between pilgrims and royal troops by the Vltava belongs to the opening of the Hussite wars. Reinforcements from western Bohemia enabled some Hussites to continue towards Prague.
quotes.source: Authored summary · references under History and sources

trivia: The three pilgrim groups, the ford location and the reinforcement turn are game reconstructions. Koranda represents religious leadership; his presence here is not treated as established.
The traditional date is 4 November 1419; a reference to St Leonard’s feast also suggests 6 November. Exact numbers and the commanders of each group remain uncertain.
zivohost.reliability: The traditional date is 4 November 1419; a reference to St Leonard’s feast also suggests 6 November. Exact numbers and the commanders of each group remain uncertain.

nekmir.name: Battle of Nekmíř
nekmir.location: Near Nekmíř fortress, 17 km NW of Plzeň

hussiteSide.composition: Infantry from Plzeň, wagons with guns and hand cannons

nekmir.terrain: Near Nekmíř. The precise location and arrangement of the wagon position are not securely known.
nekmir.outcome: Hussite victory. Wagon tactics were born.
nekmir.aftermath: Hussite victory. Wagon tactics were born.
nekmir.significance: FIRST documented use of wagon fort in history. Only 7 wagons in semicircle formation proved the concept worked.

quotes.text: Žižka’s detachment fought the Pilsen landfriede near Nekmíř. The traditional account mentions seven wagons, an early Hussite use of wagons in battle.
quotes.source: Authored summary · references under History and sources

trivia: The semicircle, wagon capabilities and both deployments serve the game. They are not a surviving battle plan.
The battle is dated to December 1419 or January 1420. It is not presented as the first use of war wagons in world history. Troop numbers are estimates.
nekmir.reliability: The battle is dated to December 1419 or January 1420. It is not presented as the first use of war wagons in world history. Troop numbers are estimates.

sudomer.name: Battle of Sudoměř
sudomer.location: Between Markovec and Škaredý fishponds, 14 km from Strakonice

enemySide.composition: Heavy cavalry, Hospitallers, squires of landfrieden

sudomer.terrain: Narrow dam between fishponds - Markovec filled, Škaredý muddy. KEY FACTOR - mud trapped dismounted knights.
sudomer.outcome: The Hussite force held off its attackers and could continue its journey.

casualties.hussites: Uncertain total; Břeněk Švihovský was killed

sudomer.aftermath: The Hussite force held off its attackers and could continue its journey.
sudomer.significance: Foundation of Žižka's reputation as undefeated commander. Proved wagon fort could defeat heavy cavalry.

quotes.text: On 25 March 1420 the retreating Hussites defended a position between the Markovec and Škaredý ponds. Terrain and wagons limited the attackers’ deployment.
quotes.source: Authored summary · references under History and sources

trivia: The map emphasizes the causeway, water and the drained pond’s mud. Token counts, attack timing and the defence duration are gameplay choices.
Accounts differ over the relative command roles of Žižka and Břeněk Švihovský. Captured and killed people must not be conflated; exact losses are unknown.
sudomer.reliability: Accounts differ over the relative command roles of Žižka and Břeněk Švihovský. Captured and killed people must not be conflated; exact losses are unknown.

vitkov.name: Battle of Vítkov

hussiteSide.strength: 26 men, 2 women and a maiden in the blockhouses; Prague relief with flails
hussiteSide.composition: Flailmen and glaivemen, few crossbows (little gunpowder), 3 women

enemySide.strength: ~30,000 total; 7-8,000 in the sector, but only ~300 riders fit into the neck

vitkov.terrain: A narrow ridge with steep sides. Fixed blockhouses and a wall restricted the attackers’ approach.
vitkov.significance: Saved Prague from the First Crusade. Became symbol of Hussite resistance and Czech national memory.

quotes.text: Jan Žižka defended Vítkov on 14 July 1420. A fixed wall and timber fieldworks formed the defences; relief from Prague struck the attackers’ flank.
quotes.source: Authored summary · references under History and sources

trivia: A fieldwork garrison is an immobile game unit, not a wagon. Unit counts and the timing of relief are simplified.
Exact casualties and the identity of the priest leading the relief are uncertain. Želivský fills that role in the game as a dramatization, not an established identification.
vitkov.reliability: Exact casualties and the identity of the priest leading the relief are uncertain. Želivský fills that role in the game as a dramatization, not an established identification.

vysehrad.name: Battle under Vyšehrad
vysehrad.location: Pankrác Plain, area around St. Pankrác church

commanders: Captains of the Prague and allied contingents
hussiteSide.composition: Praguers, Orebites, Taborites, Žatec, Louny forces

enemySide.composition: Hungarians, Germans, Silesians, Czech Catholic nobility

vysehrad.terrain: Flat plain with side ravine to Podolí. Side ravine became trap for nobility.
vysehrad.outcome: Defeat of the royal army and surrender of Vyšehrad, but not yet complete control of Prague.
vysehrad.aftermath: Defeat of the royal army and surrender of Vyšehrad, but not yet complete control of Prague.
vysehrad.significance: Destroyed backbone of Czech Catholic nobility. 25 banner lords fell. Secured Prague for Hussites.

quotes.text: The royal garrison of Vyšehrad honoured its agreement and did not join the battle on 1 November 1420. Hynek Krušina of Lichtenburg commanded the Hussites.
quotes.source: Authored summary · references under History and sources

trivia: The map retains the relationship between the castle, Vltava, Botič, Pankrác positions and Podolí slope. Distances, trenches and assault groups are not a surveyed battle plan.
The king’s exchanges with the nobles are scripted scenes, not transcripts of their words.
vysehrad.reliability: Medieval hour numbering cannot simply be rendered as 15:00. The scenario uses the expiry of the agreed deadline without claiming an exact modern time. Exact casualties remain uncertain.

kutna_hora.name: Battle of Kutná Hora
kutna_hora.location: Kutná Hora – Kaňk – the route towards Kolín

enemySide.composition: Hungarian cavalry, German and Austrian detachments

kutna_hora.terrain: Hilly countryside, strategic Kaňk hill. Terrain enabled night escape.
kutna_hora.outcome: Hussite victory. Brilliant night breakthrough with wagon fort.
kutna_hora.aftermath: Hussite victory. Brilliant night breakthrough with wagon fort.
kutna_hora.significance: FIRST mobile artillery maneuver in history - night breakthrough. Proved blind Žižka's genius.

quotes.text: After royal troops entered Kutná Hora, the Hussites were surrounded. Before dawn on 22 December 1421 they broke out with their wagons towards Kaňk and subsequently continued to Kolín.
quotes.source: Authored summary · references under History and sources

trivia: The exit zone represents the onward route beyond Kaňk. Several stages are compressed into one map; saving five detachments is a gameplay objective.
Stories about cattle driven against the wagons and Žižka’s later knighthood belong to the tradition, not the victory requirements.
kutna_hora.reliability: We do not claim an exact breakout hour, casualty count or world-first moving gunfire. Surviving accounts do not locate every wagon.

nemecky_brod.name: Battle of Německý Brod
nemecky_brod.location: Německý Brod and the Sázava crossing; Habry was an earlier clash
nemecky_brod.terrain: The town stands on the north bank of the Sázava, on the approach from Habry. Retreat continues across the river towards Jihlava.
nemecky_brod.outcome: Defeat of the retreating army and capture and devastation of Brod. Campaign-wide losses cannot be assigned to this one map.

casualties.enemy: Thousands dead in field + in city

nemecky_brod.aftermath: Defeat of the retreating army and capture and devastation of Brod. Campaign-wide losses cannot be assigned to this one map.
nemecky_brod.significance: Avenged massacre of Hussites at Kutná Hora. 548 knights drowned under ice. City empty for years.

quotes.text: After defeats near Kutná Hora and Habry, royal forces retreated towards Německý Brod. The historic town stands on the right bank of the Sázava, before the crossing along the retreat route.
quotes.source: Authored summary · references under History and sources

trivia: This is the final pursuit by the town, not Habry placed on the same battlefield. The bridge, town objective and ice crossing condense events of 8–10 January 1422.
Collapsing ice is retained as a traditional motif and gameplay risk, not an exact count of drowning victims.
nemecky_brod.reliability: Reported wagon captures and casualties vary. Tokens represent detachments, not individual people counted by a chronicler.

most.name: Battle of Most

enemySide.strength: Saxon army + Most militia + Catholic nobility

most.terrain: The surroundings of Most and Hněvín; the map is a simplified tactical layout, not a documented attack plan.
most.outcome: HUSSITE DEFEAT. Weakening of Jan Želivský's position.
most.aftermath: HUSSITE DEFEAT. Weakening of Jan Želivský's position.
most.significance: FIRST major Hussite defeat. Erased from textbooks - didn't fit image of invincible Hussites.

quotes.text: The Hussite siege of Most and Hněvín ended in defeat on 5 August 1421 after opposing reinforcements intervened.
quotes.source: Authored summary · references under History and sources

trivia: Saving the situation or taking the castle are alternative outcomes available to the player. Deployments and reinforcement turns are reconstructions.
This defeat does not prove that Hussites could never win without Žižka or wagons. Exact army composition, strengths and losses are not securely known.
most.reliability: This defeat does not prove that Hussites could never win without Žižka or wagons. Exact army composition, strengths and losses are not securely known.

usti.name: Battle of Ústí nad Labem
usti.terrain: Gentle hill with plateau. Double line of wagon fort.
usti.significance: LAST BATTLE where cavalry frontally attacked wagon fort. Piccolomini wrongly attributed victory to dead Žižka.

quotes.text: On 16 June 1426 united Hussite forces defeated their opponents near Ústí nad Labem, in the area known as Na Běhání.
quotes.source: Authored summary · references under History and sources

trivia: Two wagon lines, the attackers’ approach and the town’s proximity are compressed gameplay reconstructions, not a surveyed army deployment.
The report of only nineteen Hussite dead is presented as a chronicler’s claim, not a verified casualty tally.
usti.reliability: Army sizes and casualties vary considerably between accounts. Estimates cannot be converted into exact token counts.

tachov.name: Battle of Tachov

enemySide.composition: Crusading contingents with a wagon position

tachov.terrain: Area around Stříbro and Tachov. Indecisive - crusaders fled.
tachov.outcome: The field army collapsed in early August. The town fell on 11 August and the castle on 14 August 1427.
tachov.aftermath: The field army collapsed in early August. The town fell on 11 August and the castle on 14 August 1427.
tachov.significance: Crusades halted for 4 years. Demonstrated complete demoralization of crusader armies.

quotes.text: After retreating from Stříbro, the crusading army disintegrated near Tachov on 3–4 August 1427. A siege followed: the town fell on 11 August and the castle capitulated on 14 August.
quotes.source: Authored summary · references under History and sources

trivia: The playable pursuit ends before that siege. The epilogue describes the later stage separately.
The precise field-battle location and strengths are uncertain. Crusade numbering depends on which failed expeditions are included; we use the year instead.
tachov.reliability: The precise field-battle location and strengths are uncertain. Crusade numbering depends on which failed expeditions are included; we use the year instead.

nisa.name: Battle of Nysa (Silesia)
nisa.terrain: Before city walls. Surprise and rapid maneuver.
nisa.outcome: The Silesian campaign continued. The field engagement must not be confused with the capture of walled Nisa.
nisa.aftermath: The Silesian campaign continued. The field engagement must not be confused with the capture of walled Nisa.
nisa.significance: Part of first 'Beautiful Ride' into Silesia. Only major battle of Silesian raid - cities then surrendered without fight.

quotes.text: The 1428 campaign reached Nysa in Silesia. Fighting around the town and its suburbs must be distinguished from capturing the walled town itself.
quotes.source: Authored summary · references under History and sources

trivia: The map represents an attack on the suburb and opposing field force. Taking the entire walled town is not treated as an established outcome of this episode.
The consulted accounts do not agree on detailed deployments, strengths or the exact March date. This is a loose reconstruction, not a verified battlefield plan.
nisa.reliability: The consulted accounts do not agree on detailed deployments, strengths or the exact March date. This is a loose reconstruction, not a verified battlefield plan.

domazlice.name: Battle of Domažlice
domazlice.location: Between Domažlice and Kdyně, at Baldov hill

hussiteSide.composition: Combined unions of Taborites, Orphans and Praguers

enemySide.composition: Several thousand wagons in Hussite style (9,000 planned), hundreds of guns

domazlice.terrain: Road to Domažlice, Všeruby pass. Pass - narrow bottleneck for fleeing.
domazlice.outcome: The expedition’s collapse accelerated the turn towards negotiation. Panic did not prevent some units from resisting.
domazlice.aftermath: The expedition’s collapse accelerated the turn towards negotiation. Panic did not prevent some units from resisting.
domazlice.significance: Peak of Hussite glory. Largest crusade fled without daring to fight. CARDINAL'S HAT lost in flight became symbol.

quotes.text: On 14 August 1431 the Hussites came to relieve besieged Domažlice. Panic and flight overtook the crusading army, although some troops still fought.
quotes.source: Authored summary · references under History and sources

trivia: In the game the hymn amplifies the fear of an already uncertain army. Disrupted command and misread troop movements provide context, rather than a single miraculous trigger.
The idea that the song alone won the whole battle without any fighting belongs to legend.
domazlice.reliability: The respective effects of reports, movements and sounds cannot be measured. Army strengths and casualties are not presented as certain totals.

lipany.name: Battle of Lipany
lipany.location: Between Hřiby and Lipská hora, 40 km E of Prague
lipany.terrain: Lipská hora (more advantageous for radicals), plain at Hřiby. TWO ARMIES IN WAGON FORTS facing each other.
lipany.outcome: Crushing defeat of radicals. End of field armies. Compactata at Jihlava 1436.

casualties.hussites: Heavy; totals and numbers of executed prisoners disputed

lipany.aftermath: Crushing defeat of radicals. End of field armies. Compactata at Jihlava 1436.
lipany.significance: End of radical Hussitism. Fratricidal battle where Hussites defeated Hussites. 'Czechs can be defeated only by Czechs.'

quotes.text: On 30 May 1434 Hussite radicals fought a coalition of Catholics and moderate Utraquists. Defeat gravely weakened the field armies; it did not instantly end all fighting.
quotes.source: Authored summary · references under History and sources

trivia: The ruse and the decision to leave the wagon position are translated into a few turns. A radical victory is explicitly alternative history.
Stories of prisoners burned in barns cannot simply be converted into a precise additional death count.
lipany.reliability: The locations of individual formations remain a subject of archaeological research. Estimates of losses and prisoners are not a single verified tally.

horice.name: Battle of Hořice
horice.location: Gothard hill (357 m), SE of Hořice in Jičín region

enemySide.composition: Cavalry formations of Catholic Czech nobility

horice.terrain: Gothard hill. Wagon fort on hilltop.
horice.outcome: Crushing Orebite victory. Showed strength of eastern Bohemian Hussites.
horice.aftermath: Crushing Orebite victory. Showed strength of eastern Bohemian Hussites.
horice.significance: FIRST INTERNAL CONFLICT OF HUSSITES. Eastern Bohemia = cradle of Hussite commanders.

quotes.text: Žižka’s army fought Čeněk of Vartenberk’s force near Hořice in April 1423; Gothard hill is central to reconstructions of the battle.
quotes.source: Authored summary · references under History and sources

trivia: The scenario models a hill defence with wagons and missile troops. Dismounting, counterattack timing and the commander roster are gameplay reconstructions.
The exact April date varies in the literature. A detailed deployment plan and precise numbers are unavailable; calling this the first internal Hussite conflict would be misleading.
horice.reliability: The exact April date varies in the literature. A detailed deployment plan and precise numbers are unavailable; calling this the first internal Hussite conflict would be misleading.

malesov.name: Battle of Malešov
malesov.location: At Malešov fortress, 6 km S of Kutná Hora, valley of Bohynka stream

enemySide.composition: Prague union + Plzeň landfrieden + moderate Utraquists

malesov.terrain: A possible reconstruction of a slope and valley near Malešov with a wagon position; the precise battlefield is unknown.
malesov.outcome: A major victory for Žižka over his opponents’ coalition. The battlefield’s precise location is unknown.

casualties.enemy: Chroniclers’ estimates; no secure split between the two sides

malesov.aftermath: A major victory for Žižka over his opponents’ coalition. The battlefield’s precise location is unknown.
malesov.significance: Peak of Žižka's career - blind defeated superior numbers. Coalition attempted ASSASSINATION of Žižka. Žižka died 4 months later (October 11, 1424).

quotes.text: On 7 June 1424 Žižka defeated a coalition of Prague forces and Catholics near Malešov. Scholarship allows for wagons blocking a valley followed by a counterattack.
quotes.source: Authored summary · references under History and sources

trivia: The Bohynka stream, slope and deployments are one possible reconstruction. Conditional panic represents disruption of the column’s leading ranks, not stone-filled wagons.
Wagons rolled downhill with stones appear in a later annalistic tradition. Jan Biederman considers their use highly improbable.
malesov.reliability: The exact battlefield and opposing commander are not securely identified. Diviš Bořek is a gameplay casting choice; a precise 1,200-to-200 casualty split is not an established tally.
